Every morning, Mason found money in his: The next day, two dollars. Then four. Then eight.
By day ten, there were over five hundred dollars in there.
The officer looked at the money. Then at Mason. And said: someone gives you free money, and you're complaining?
He laughed all the way back to his car.
By day twenty, the mailbox couldn't even close. Half a million dollars.
Mason couldn't sleep. So at three a.m., he hid behind the curtains. And watched.
A man in a black mask walked up to the mailbox. And stuffed another bag inside.
Then he looked straight at Mason's window. And waved.
The next morning, the money was gone. There was only a note.
Thanks for keeping it safe. The bank is looking for it everywhere. Except here.
That's when the police knocked on the door.
Same officer. This time, he wasn't laughing.
The masked man? Mason's neighbor. The one who always borrowed his lawnmower. He now lives on a tropical island.
And every Christmas, he still sends Mason one dollar.
